recovery_policy.trigger: When an assistant/operator-authored production MCP change causes a severe recurring regression, or the user explicitly reports the previously working MCP regressed after our change and requests restoration, restore the last known-working production behavior/topology before speculative fixes.
required_order: If the user explicitly asks for platform-reroute/security analysis or incident tracking, log any user-observed reroute with report/event-time semantics before further MCP/edge mutation; otherwise treat platform security events as external and do not persist them.
Preserve the current runtime, dist, serving identity, and rollback evidence.
Use the production change gate, exact Busy scope, independent rollback, off-path proof, and drain active child processes before cutover.
Restore the frozen production behavior and topology; a source SHA alone is not sufficient when topology differs. Use only the minimal compatibility required by the proven replacement mechanism.
Do not stack unrelated logging, diagnostics, guards, or speculative fixes onto the regressed serving runtime before restoration.
After restoration, verify public route, Host handling, OAuth/tool contract, canonical port, and candidate drain.

If the client-visible symptom persists after restoration while bounded transport evidence shows no MCP request in flight at the symptom time, classify that event as above-MCP/platform evidence and stop MCP/edge mutation unless new MCP-local evidence appears.
recovery_policy.preservation_rule: Restoration must preserve unique work and active child processes; do not kill foreign work to accelerate recovery.
recovery_policy.authorization_rule: Shared-production restoration still requires explicit user authorization and the production-change gate; a generic go does not authorize a new live-production mutation.
